headword: {源氏物語|げんじものがたり}

definitions.explanation: A long prose tale of the Heian imperial court written in the early eleventh century by the court lady {紫式部|むらさきしきぶ}. It follows the loves and career of the prince {光源氏|ひかるげんじ} and his descendants, and is often called the world's oldest novel.

examples.japanese: {源氏物語|げんじものがたり}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}んだ→読む：00426_yomu⟧。
examples.english: I read The Tale of Genji.

examples.japanese: {源氏物語|げんじものがたり}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{紫式部|むらさきしきぶ}→紫式部：30771_murasakishikibu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{書|か}いた→書く：00477_kaku⟧。
examples.english: The Tale of Genji was written by Murasaki Shikibu.

examples.english: The original is difficult, so many people enjoy The Tale of Genji in modern translations or manga.

notes:
Often shortened to ⟦{源氏|げんじ}→源氏：16644_genji⟧ in literary talk. It has 54 chapters, counted with the counter {帖|じょう}.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {光源氏|ひかるげんじ}: the Shining Genji, the hero; also used jokingly for a handsome, popular man
- {源氏物語|げんじものがたり}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{世界|せかい}→世界：01447_sekai⟧: the world of the Heian court
- {現代語訳|げんだいごやく}: modern-Japanese translation (famous ones by Yosano Akiko and Tanizaki Jun'ichirō)

CULTURAL NOTE:
It is standard material in high-school classical Japanese, and its aesthetic of ⟦{物|もの}の{哀|あわ}れ→物の哀れ：30312_mononoaware⟧, a gentle sadness at the passing of things, shaped later Japanese literature. A scene from the illustrated scrolls appears on the back of the 2,000-yen note.
